insights.topic: Deterministic purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: The network has cryptographically verified 11,932 purchase events totaling $971K in GMV — each receipt is a confirmed transaction, not an inferred intent signal. That is a structurally different input for targeting than cookie-based or behavioral inference models.

insights.topic: Unknown/digital category is the largest GMV bucket
insights.insight: The 'Unknown' category accounts for $109,460 — 29.3% of 14-day GMV — and is almost certainly SaaS and digital subscription spend based on the DKIM vendor list (OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad). Brands selling software, subscriptions, or digital products have a verified-spend audience here that physical-retail targeting misses entirely.

insights.topic: Automotive parts as a durable verified-spend category
insights.insight: NAPA Auto Parts ranks second by receipt count at 87 receipts in 14 days, behind only Walmart at 181 — it is not a one-cycle anomaly. Automotive aftermarket is an established, recurring share of verified spend in this network, relevant to any brand targeting vehicle owners or home improvement buyers.

The network has expanded to confirmed non-metro CBSAs across Maine, Tennessee, Missouri, Idaho, Nebraska, Iowa, Wisconsin, North Carolina, and Rhode Island — markets where digital ad targeting is notoriously thin and third-party data is weakest. Verified purchase signals in these geographies are comparatively rare and therefore higher-value.

insights.topic: Velocity contraction is a structural signal, not noise
insights.insight: Token velocity has dropped to 0.944x with acceleration at 0.999x — the first sub-1.0x reading since the April 12 peak — meaning week-over-week throughput is now contracting. CMOs evaluating this network for scale should track whether this is post-expansion consolidation (consistent with the observed pulse pattern) or the beginning of a sustained slowdown.

insights.topic: Warehouse and mass-market retail anchor the receipt base
insights.insight: Walmart (181 receipts) and Costco (63 receipts) together represent a high-frequency, high-basket-size consumer segment within the verified pool. For CPG and household brands, these receipts identify actual buyers at the two largest US retailers — without relying on retailer data-sharing agreements.
